- If sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- If sentiment is strongly bearish (≤ -0.50), model often underestimates downside; add buffer or adjust downward bias.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior day), model frequently overshoots; apply decay or smoothing to subsequent forecasts.
- When sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish (or vice versa) within 3–5 days, model fails to adjust quickly; introduce sentiment-weighted lag correction.
- Model consistently underestimates true mean reversion in 30-day horizon; apply mean-reversion bias toward historical 18-day average if sentiment is neutral or mixed.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.00–0.33) and price is trending, model often fails to capture momentum; increase sensitivity to recent price movement.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome deviates >5% from 18-day average, adjust forecast to align with sentiment-driven mean reversion or volatility shift.
